name: DLL Hijacking Detection via Sysmon Event 7
command: Get-WinEvent -Path 'C:\Logs\DLLHijack\sysmon.evtx' | Where-Object {$_.Id -eq 7} | Select-Object TimeCreated, Message | Format-List
description: Detect DLL hijacking attacks using Sysmon Event ID 7 (ImageLoad). DLL hijacking occurs when a legitimate application loads a malicious DLL from an attacker-controlled path instead of the intended system path.
source: CDSA Module 03: Windows Event Logs & Finding Evil
notes:
DLL Search Order Hijacking (how the attack works):
  Windows loads DLLs in this order:
    1. Directory of the executable
    2. System directory (C:\Windows\System32)
    3. Windows directory (C:\Windows)
    4. Current directory
    5. PATH entries
  Attacker: places malicious DLL with a legitimate name in a directory
    searched BEFORE the real DLL location.

Sysmon Event ID 7 (ImageLoad) key fields:
  Image         → the process loading the DLL
  ImageLoaded   → full path of the DLL that was loaded
  Hashes        → MD5, SHA256, ImpHash of loaded DLL
  Signed        → true/false — is the DLL signed?
  Signature     → signing certificate / vendor
  SignatureStatus → Valid, Expired, Revoked, Unchecked

Detection IOCs:
  → Signed=false for a DLL that should always be signed (e.g. Windows system DLLs)
  → ImageLoaded path outside System32 for a known system DLL name
  → Same DLL name loaded from two different paths across processes
  → Low/no-reputation DLL loaded by high-privilege process
  → ImpHash matches known malware family

Lab analysis path: C:\Logs\DLLHijack\
  → Contains sysmon.evtx with DLL hijack evidence
  → Look for Event 7 where Signed=false or ImageLoaded path is suspicious

XML query for unsigned DLL loads:
  $query = @'
  <QueryList><Query Id="0">
    <Select Path="Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational">
      *[System[EventID=7]] and *[EventData[Data[@Name='Signed']='false']]
    </Select>
  </Query></QueryList>
  '@
  Get-WinEvent -FilterXml $query

examples.label: Read DLLHijack lab evtx — all Event 7 (ImageLoad) events
examples.command: Get-WinEvent -Path 'C:\Logs\DLLHijack\sysmon.evtx' | Where-Object {$_.Id -eq 7} | Select-Object TimeCreated, Message | Format-List

examples.label: Filter Event 7 for unsigned DLL loads from live Sysmon log
examples.command: Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' -FilterXPath "*[System[EventID=7] and EventData[Data[@Name='Signed']='false']]" | Select-Object TimeCreated, Message | Format-List

examples.label: Parse Event 7 XML to extract Image, ImageLoaded, Signed fields
examples.command: Get-WinEvent -Path 'C:\Logs\DLLHijack\sysmon.evtx' | Where-Object {$_.Id -eq 7} | ForEach-Object { $xml=[xml]$_.ToXml(); $data=$xml.Event.EventData.Data; [PSCustomObject]@{Time=$_.TimeCreated; Process=($data|?{$_.Name -eq 'Image'}).'#text'; DLL=($data|?{$_.Name -eq 'ImageLoaded'}).'#text'; Signed=($data|?{$_.Name -eq 'Signed'}).'#text'} } | Format-Table -AutoSize

examples.label: FilterXml query for unsigned DLL loads
